D011-D012_h005.question_both:
Um… so I guess the main thing is I feel on edge a lot, like my body’s stuck in “go” mode. Even when I’m just sitting in class, I’m kind of buzzing in my seat, like I can’t fully relax. My shoulders and the back of my neck are always tight, almost like I’ve been shrugging for hours. I get these dull headaches from it a few times a week.

My brain kind of runs away with stuff. If I miss one homework problem or say something awkward, I’ll immediately start thinking, “What if this tanks my grade, what if colleges see this, what if I screw everything up?” It sounds dumb when I say it, but in the moment it feels really real. Those thoughts just shove themselves in when I’m trying to focus—like I’ll be doing a test or driving practice and suddenly I’m stuck on some “what if” scenario and lose my place.

There’s also this one thing—this particular situation—that really sets me off. Just thinking about being in it makes my chest feel tight and my muscles clench up more. But it’s not like that’s the only time I’m tense; it’s just worse then. This has been going on for at least the last few months, kind of gradually getting more noticeable.
D011-D012_h005.question_a:
It’s kind of like my brain is always running disaster scenarios, about everything. It’s been this way for at least the past year, but way worse the last 6–8 months. If I get a B on a quiz, I immediately jump to, “I’m going to fail the class, not get into college, ruin my life.” If my mom is five minutes late picking me up, I’m sure she’s been in a car crash. I worry about school, my little sister, money, my health, even random stuff like the house catching on fire.

These thoughts just slam into my head when I’m trying to do homework or take a test and I lose my train of thought. Even when nothing is happening, I feel wired, like I’m buzzing inside and can’t relax or sit still. My shoulders and neck are constantly tight and sore, and I get headaches from clenching up all day.

I do have a big thing about dogs — if I see one off-leash I get really freaked out and avoid that street — but the anxiety isn’t just about that. It feels like it’s spread into pretty much every part of my life.
D011-D012_h005.question_b:
It’s mostly this one thing that sets me off. I’m fine in most situations—tests, talking to people, even thinking about college—but whenever I know I might have to get on a plane, I just lose it.

It started about a year ago, when my parents began talking about flying out to visit colleges. As soon as anything about flying comes up—seeing planes in movies, hearing someone mention airports—I start imagining the worst: the plane breaking in half, falling out of the sky, me dying and my parents watching it on the news. I know it sounds over the top, but in the moment it feels like it’s definitely going to happen.

When I’m thinking about it, I get so wound up I can’t sit still. My mind keeps jumping back to it even if I’m trying to do homework or play video games. My shoulders and neck lock up and ache, and sometimes I get these tension headaches. But outside of that—like day-to-day school stuff or my health—I don’t really worry. It’s pretty much just this flying thing that completely takes over.

I’ll be sketching or pinning a bodice, and the tiniest noise in the studio—a zipper dropping, someone laughing suddenly—makes me jump. My assistant jokes that I’m “skittish,” but it doesn’t feel funny to me.

I do worry a lot, but it kind of bounces around. One minute I’m thinking about a client’s deadline, then my rent, then whether something’s wrong with my mum even though she’s fine, then back to whether I messed up an order. It’s not always about the same thing; it just sort of shifts.

Sleep hasn’t been great. Technically I’m in bed enough hours, but I wake up feeling like I didn’t really rest, like my body never fully powered down. Then I go into fittings already tired and wired.

There’s also this one thing that really sets me off—when I have to deal with [that specific thing/situation], I get especially tense and my mind races. But even outside of that, I still feel this low-level nervous buzz running in the background most days.
D011-D012_h006.question_a:
It feels like my whole life is just… buzzing with worry all the time. It’s not just one thing. I wake up already tense, thinking about deadlines for clients, whether a seam will come undone during someone’s walk down the aisle, if a shipment of lace will get stuck in customs, if I’m saving enough for the future, if my mom is okay alone, even if my landlord might suddenly raise the rent. My brain just jumps from one “what if” to another all day.

I do sleep, like 7–8 hours most nights, but I wake up exhausted, like I didn’t rest at all. My body feels tight, and the smallest noise—my phone buzzing, a car door slamming—makes me jump. At the studio, if a client suddenly calls my name or drops a hanger, I feel this jolt in my chest.

I am really scared of flying specifically—I’ll avoid destination weddings that require travel if I can—but it’s not only that. Even when I’m nowhere near an airport, I still feel constantly on edge and worried about a hundred other things. This has been going on for at least the last year and a half, maybe longer.
D011-D012_h006.question_b:
It’s really just one thing that sets me off: flying.

I’m fine most of the time at work sketching gowns or fitting brides. I don’t sit around worrying about money or my family or health. But the second I know I have to get on a plane—even just seeing a flight confirmation email—my body goes into overdrive. My heart races, my hands shake, and I can’t stop picturing the plane falling out of the sky. I’ll obsess over every tiny sound it might make, every bump of turbulence, to the point that I’ll cancel trips or drive for hours rather than fly.

This has been going on for at least a couple of years, getting worse with each trip I have to take for bridal shows. The week before a flight I’m jumpy; even small noises in my apartment make me startle. I sleep 7–8 hours, but I wake up feeling like I didn’t rest at all, because I’ve spent the night half-awake, replaying what could go wrong on the plane. Outside of anything to do with flying, though, I don’t feel anxious.

I guess this has been going on for… maybe a few months? It’s hard to pin down exactly. My wife keeps saying I’ve changed. I feel on edge most of the time, like I’m bracing for something bad, even when I’m just sitting in my chair reading the paper. The smallest noise—the kettle whistling, a car door slamming—makes me jump. It’s silly, but if I misplace a bill or forget an appointment, my mind goes straight to “this will cause huge problems,” like we’ll lose the house or something, even though I know that’s unlikely.

Sleep is strange. You’d think I’d be up worrying all night, but instead I’m sleeping more than I used to. I stay in bed late, doze in the afternoon in my armchair, and still feel tired. 

There’s one thing that really sets me off: going over that old bridge near our place. I start imagining it collapsing, us going over the edge. Sometimes I avoid it entirely, take the long way round. I’m not sure if that’s just me being cautious or part of whatever this is.
D011-D012_h007.question_a:
I’ve been on edge for at least the past year, pretty much every day. It’s not just one thing. I lie in bed thinking something terrible is going to happen to my wife, or that our pension will suddenly disappear, or that the children will have some accident on the road. If I misplace a bill or forget an appointment, my mind jumps straight to, “We’ll lose the house,” or “They’ll think I’m incompetent and something awful will follow.” It feels like any small slip will snowball into disaster.

I also worry an unreasonable amount about my health — every ache, I start thinking it’s a stroke or cancer. I know, logically, it’s probably nothing, but I can’t switch it off. Even simple things like going to the dentist or being in a crowded supermarket make me tense and shaky; I dread them for days beforehand.

Because of all this, I end up sleeping far too much. I can easily sleep 10–11 hours at night and still doze off in the afternoon, but I never feel rested. Little noises, like the kettle clicking off or a car door slamming, make me jump. My nerves feel frayed all the time, across everything in my life.
D011-D012_h007.question_b:
It’s really just this one thing that sets me off: bridges. Driving over them, walking under them, even seeing one on the news. The rest of my life is fairly calm—I’m retired, I read the paper, putter around the garden—but if I know we have to cross a bridge, I start going to pieces.

For the past couple of years, any time my wife suggests visiting our son across town, my mind jumps straight to disaster. I picture the bridge collapsing, the car going over the edge, us trapped in the water. It feels ridiculous, but in the moment it seems completely certain. I start sweating, my heart races, and I can’t think about anything else until I find a way to avoid that route.

Otherwise I’m not lying awake worrying about my health or money or the grandchildren. In fact, I’ve been sleeping more than usual—dozing off in the afternoon and still sleeping long at night, especially after I’ve had a scare about a bridge. I’m jittery too: a car backfiring or the creak of the house makes me jump, but it’s worst if it reminds me of traffic on a bridge.
